question: What is the main problem in the body when someone has anaemia?

options.A: Increased thickness of the blood plasma
options.D: Reduced oxygen-carrying capacity of the blood

explanation: You've got this! Anaemia simply means the blood doesn't have enough red blood cells or hemoglobin to carry the oxygen your body needs to function well. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T6#GNS311_U2_T6_h1)

question: Why does a person's heart beat faster when they have severe anaemia?

options.A: To warm up body tissues chilled by slow blood flow
options.B: To compensate for lower oxygen delivery by pumping blood faster
options.C: To lower high blood pressure from extra red blood cells
options.D: To help the kidneys filter out waste quickly

explanation: Think of it this way: since each drop of blood carries less oxygen, the heart has to pump much faster to make sure vital organs get what they need! [learn more](GNS311_U2_T6#GNS311_U2_T6_h1)

question: What is the most common nutritional shortage that causes microcytic anaemia?
explanation: Great to know for clinicals! Without enough iron, the body cannot build proper hemoglobin, leaving red blood cells looking small and pale. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T6#GNS311_U2_T6_h2)

question: Lab results show a patient has large (macrocytic) red blood cells. Which vitamin shortage should you check for first?
explanation: Spot on! Vitamins B12 and folate act like master builders for DNA during red blood cell growth. Without them, the cells grow too large instead of maturing properly. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T6#GNS311_U2_T6_h2)

question: What is the most common sign you will hear patients complain about when they have anaemia?
explanation: Makes total sense, right? When tissues are starved of oxygen, patients will constantly feel tired, heavy-limbed, and lacking in energy. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T6#GNS311_U2_T6_h3)

question: Why do patients with anaemia often have very pale skin and nail beds?

options.A: There is less red hemoglobin pigment in surface blood vessels
options.B: Blood is completely blocked from reaching the skin surface
options.C: The skin makes extra melanin to protect itself
options.D: Poor circulation causes fluid to collect under the skin

explanation: Hemoglobin is what paints our blood red. When levels drop, that healthy pink color fades from places close to the surface, like the palms, gums, and nail beds. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T6#GNS311_U2_T6_h3)

question: Which standard lab test checks a patient's hemoglobin and hematocrit levels directly?
explanation: The good old Full Blood Count (or Complete Blood Count) is your go-to test for looking at red cells, hemoglobin, and all things blood-related in the ward! [learn more](GNS311_U2_T6#GNS311_U2_T6_h4)

question: What does a serum ferritin blood test tell the healthcare team?
explanation: Think of ferritin as the body's iron savings account. A serum ferritin test lets you see how much iron is safely tucked away in storage. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T6#GNS311_U2_T6_h4)

question: What is the primary goal when treating a patient with anaemia?

options.A: To identify and treat the underlying cause
options.B: To permanently stop all dietary iron intake
options.C: To permanently increase the white blood cell count
options.D: To lower the body temperature to resting levels

explanation: You can't just slap a band-aid on anaemia! Finding out *why* it's happening—whether it's blood loss, heavy periods, or poor nutrition—is key to fixing it. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T6#GNS311_U2_T6_h5)

question: A patient is taking oral iron pills. What advice should you give them to help their body absorb the iron better?

options.A: Take the supplement with vitamin C or orange juice
options.B: Crush the pills and mix them into a yogurt meal
options.C: Swallow the tablets immediately after drinking a glass of milk
options.D: Take the medication right before going to sleep at night

explanation: Vitamin C is iron's best friend! It creates an acidic environment in the stomach that helps the body absorb oral iron much more effectively. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T6#GNS311_U2_T6_h5)

question: Why should you schedule planned rest breaks for a hospitalized patient with severe anaemia?

options.A: To lower blood pressure before giving medications
options.B: To give the digestive tract time to process iron pills
options.C: To prevent blood clots from forming in the legs
options.D: To reduce the overall oxygen demand on the body

explanation: Resting lowers the body's workload, which saves precious oxygen for a patient who tires out easily. Pacing is key in nursing care! [learn more](GNS311_U2_T6#GNS311_U2_T6_h6)

question: What is your most important duty during the first fifteen minutes of a blood transfusion?

options.A: Elevate the head of the bed to a high Fowler position
options.B: Flush the intravenous tubing quickly with dextrose solution
options.C: Stay with the patient and monitor for acute transfusion reactions
options.D: Draw another blood sample from a peripheral vein

explanation: Safety first! Most dangerous transfusion reactions happen right at the beginning, so staying by the bedside to watch your patient is a must. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T6#GNS311_U2_T6_h6)

question: What serious long-term problem can happen if severe, chronic anaemia is ignored?
explanation: If the heart is forced to pump extra fast for months or years to move oxygen-poor blood, the heart muscle eventually gets exhausted and begins to fail. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T6#GNS311_U2_T6_h7)

question: A patient calls the clinic panicking because their stool turned dark green after starting iron pills. What should you tell them?

options.A: Advise them to stop taking the iron tablets immediately and rush to the hospital
options.B: Reassure them that this is a harmless and expected side effect
options.C: Tell them to collect a stool sample to check for bleeding
options.D: Tell them to drink less water because it dilutes the drug

explanation: No need to panic! Unabsorbed iron naturally turns the stool dark green or black as it passes through. Giving this quick reassurance eases patient anxiety instantly. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T6#GNS311_U2_T6_h7)
